questions.question: What does a trunk link do?
choices: Connects a PC to a switch
questions.explanation: A trunk carries traffic for multiple VLANs between switches using 802.1Q.

correct.explanation: A trunk tags frames with 802.1Q VLAN IDs so multiple VLANs cross one inter-switch link.

incorrect.explanation: Access ports carry a single VLAN untagged — trunks carry many VLANs with tags.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Describing access-port behavior on a trunk question
incorrect.whatItDoes: Carries one VLAN only points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for trunk purpose.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "trunk purpose", Carries multiple VLANs between switches satisfies what this question tests — Carries one VLAN only does not.

incorrect.explanation: PC-to-switch links are access ports — trunks connect switches (or switch to router-on-a-stick).
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using end-host access link for trunk definition
incorrect.whatItDoes: Connects a PC to a switch points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for trunk purpose.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "trunk purpose", Carries multiple VLANs between switches satisfies what this question tests — Connects a PC to a switch does not.

incorrect.explanation: Routing between VLANs needs a Layer 3 device — trunks extend Layer 2 VLANs across links, not route them.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting trunk to route between VLANs
incorrect.whatItDoes: Routes between VLANs points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for trunk purpose.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "trunk purpose", Carries multiple VLANs between switches satisfies what this question tests — Routes between VLANs does not.

answerReview.examTip: Trunk = 802.1Q tags on inter-switch links; native VLAN must match both ends.

questions.question: How big is the 802.1Q tag added to a frame?
questions.explanation: The 802.1Q tag is 4 bytes and contains the 12-bit VLAN ID.

correct.explanation: The 802.1Q tag is 4 bytes inserted into the Ethernet frame.

incorrect.explanation: 2 bytes is too small — 802.1Q adds 4 bytes (TPID + PCP/DEI + VLAN ID).
incorrect.misconceptionTested: 802.1Q tag is 2 bytes
incorrect.whatItDoes: 2 bytes points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for tag size.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "tag size", 4 bytes satisfies what this question tests — 2 bytes does not.

incorrect.explanation: 8 bytes describes something else — 802.1Q is exactly 4 bytes.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: 802.1Q tag is 8 bytes
incorrect.whatItDoes: 8 bytes points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for tag size.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "tag size", 4 bytes satisfies what this question tests — 8 bytes does not.

incorrect.explanation: 12 bytes is not the 802.1Q tag size — it's 4 bytes.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: 802.1Q tag is 12 bytes
incorrect.whatItDoes: 12 bytes points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for tag size.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "tag size", 4 bytes satisfies what this question tests — 12 bytes does not.

answerReview.examTip: 802.1Q frame: DA + SA + 4-byte tag + Type/Len + Data + FCS — native VLAN frames are untagged.

questions.question: On an 802.1Q trunk, how is the native VLAN’s traffic sent?
questions.explanation: Native VLAN frames cross the trunk untagged.

correct.explanation: Native VLAN frames cross an 802.1Q trunk untagged — all other VLANs are tagged with their VLAN ID.

incorrect.explanation: Double-tagging (Q-in-Q) is a provider technique — standard native VLAN traffic is sent with no 802.1Q tag.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Applying Q-in-Q to standard native VLAN behavior
incorrect.whatItDoes: Double-tagged expects VLAN tags on a link that should behave as access-only in this stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: This stem (native vlan) targets access-port behavior — Untagged is correct; Double-tagged applies trunk tagging where a single VLAN is expected.

incorrect.explanation: Tagged frames carry an 802.1Q header — only non-native VLANs are tagged on a trunk.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Tagging native VLAN traffic like all other VLANs
incorrect.whatItDoes: Tagged expects VLAN tags on a link that should behave as access-only in this stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: This stem (native vlan) targets access-port behavior — Untagged is correct; Tagged applies trunk tagging where a single VLAN is expected.

incorrect.explanation: Native VLAN traffic is forwarded normally — it is not dropped for lacking a tag.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Assuming untagged native VLAN frames are discarded
incorrect.whatItDoes: Dropped implies the device should discard the frame instead of forwarding or flooding it.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "native vlan", Untagged satisfies what this question tests — Dropped does not.

answerReview.examTip: Trunk rule: native VLAN = untagged; all others tagged. Match native VLAN both ends.

questions.question: Two trunked switches log a native VLAN mismatch. What is the likely effect?
choices: Traffic from those VLANs can leak/merge
questions.explanation: A native VLAN mismatch can merge the two native VLANs’ traffic and triggers a CDP warning.

correct.explanation: Native VLAN mismatch puts each switch's untagged traffic into the peer's native VLAN — traffic can leak between VLANs and CDP reports the error.

incorrect.explanation: Trunk speed is negotiated separately — native VLAN mismatch affects which VLAN receives untagged frames, not link speed.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing VLAN mismatch with speed/duplex issues
incorrect.whatItDoes: Trunk speed drops implies the device should discard the frame instead of forwarding or flooding it.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "native mismatch", Traffic from those VLANs can leak/merge satisfies what this question tests — Trunk speed drops does not.

incorrect.explanation: Tagged VLANs still work on a mismatched native VLAN trunk — the problem is untagged traffic landing in the wrong VLAN, not a total trunk shutdown.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting all VLANs to fail when only native is mismatched
incorrect.whatItDoes: All VLANs stop points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for native mismatch.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "native mismatch", Traffic from those VLANs can leak/merge satisfies what this question tests — All VLANs stop does not.

incorrect.explanation: CDP logs %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH because the misconfiguration has real forwarding impact — it is not cosmetic.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Treating native VLAN mismatch as harmless warning
incorrect.whatItDoes: Nothing — it is cosmetic points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for native mismatch.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "native mismatch", Traffic from those VLANs can leak/merge satisfies what this question tests — Nothing — it is cosmetic does not.

answerReview.examTip: Native VLAN mismatch → untagged traffic bleeds into wrong VLAN. Fix both ends.

questions.question: Which command forces a port to trunk?
questions.explanation: switchport mode trunk sets the port to trunking.

correct.explanation: switchport mode trunk forces the port to operate as an 802.1Q trunk regardless of DTP negotiation.

incorrect.explanation: switchport mode access keeps the port in access mode — it will not carry multiple VLANs as a trunk.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting access mode when trunk is required
incorrect.whatItDoes: switchport mode access points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for config trunk.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "config trunk", switchport mode trunk satisfies what this question tests — switchport mode access does not.

incorrect.explanation: switchport trunk allowed vlan filters which VLANs cross the trunk — it does not change the port to trunk mode by itself.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Believing allowed-VLAN command sets trunk mode
incorrect.whatItDoes: switchport trunk allowed vlan expects VLAN tags on a link that should behave as access-only in this stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "config trunk", switchport mode trunk satisfies what this question tests — switchport trunk allowed vlan does not.

incorrect.explanation: switchport nonegotiate disables DTP but does not force trunk — you still need switchport mode trunk (or dynamic desirable/auto).
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Equating nonegotiate with forcing trunk mode
incorrect.whatItDoes: switchport nonegotiate points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for config trunk.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "config trunk", switchport mode trunk satisfies what this question tests — switchport nonegotiate does not.

answerReview.examTip: Force trunk → switchport mode trunk (then tune allowed/native VLANs).

questions.question: Which command disables DTP auto-negotiation on a port?
questions.explanation: switchport nonegotiate stops DTP, a hardening best practice.

correct.explanation: switchport nonegotiate stops DTP from sending negotiation frames — the port stays in whatever mode you configured manually.

incorrect.explanation: no dtp is not standard IOS trunk syntax — DTP is disabled per interface with switchport nonegotiate.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Inventing global no dtp command
incorrect.whatItDoes: no dtp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for DTP security.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "DTP security", switchport nonegotiate satisfies what this question tests — no dtp does not.

incorrect.explanation: switchport mode dynamic participates in DTP negotiation — it does not disable auto-negotiation.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using dynamic mode to stop DTP
incorrect.whatItDoes: switchport mode dynamic points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for DTP security.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "DTP security", switchport nonegotiate satisfies what this question tests — switchport mode dynamic does not.

incorrect.explanation: no switchport trunk is not the command to disable DTP — use switchport nonegotiate on the interface.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Negating switchport trunk instead of nonegotiate
incorrect.whatItDoes: no switchport trunk expects VLAN tags on a link that should behave as access-only in this stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "DTP security", switchport nonegotiate satisfies what this question tests — no switchport trunk does not.

answerReview.examTip: Disable DTP on a trunk → switchport nonegotiate after setting the mode.

questions.question: Which command shows trunk mode, native VLAN, and allowed VLANs?
questions.explanation: show interfaces trunk lists trunking details.

correct.explanation: show interfaces trunk lists trunking status, native VLAN, and allowed VLANs per trunk interface.

incorrect.explanation: show vlan brief lists VLAN IDs and port assignments — it does not show trunk encapsulation, native VLAN, or allowed lists.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using VLAN brief for trunk operational detail
incorrect.whatItDoes: show vlan brief is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (verify trunk): show interfaces trunk inspects the right table or state — show vlan brief shows unrelated information.

incorrect.explanation: show ip interface brief summarizes Layer 3 status — trunk mode and allowed VLANs are Layer 2 trunk parameters.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Checking IP brief for trunk VLAN details
incorrect.whatItDoes: show ip interface brief is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (verify trunk): show interfaces trunk inspects the right table or state — show ip interface brief shows unrelated information.

incorrect.explanation: show cdp neighbors discovers adjacent devices — it does not report 802.1Q trunk configuration.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using CDP neighbors for trunk verification
incorrect.whatItDoes: show cdp neighbors is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (verify trunk): show interfaces trunk inspects the right table or state — show cdp neighbors shows unrelated information.

questions.question: Which command limits a trunk to VLANs 10 and 20?
questions.explanation: switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 prunes the trunk.

correct.explanation: switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 restricts the trunk to only VLANs 10 and 20.

incorrect.explanation: switchport access vlan sets an access port — not trunk allowed list.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: access vlan on trunk limit
incorrect.whatItDoes: switchport access vlan 10,20 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for allowed vlans.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "allowed vlans", switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 satisfies what this question tests — switchport access vlan 10,20 does not.

incorrect.explanation: vlan 10,20 creates VLANs — doesn't filter a trunk allowed list.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: vlan command limits trunk
incorrect.whatItDoes: vlan 10,20 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for allowed vlans.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "allowed vlans", switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 satisfies what this question tests — vlan 10,20 does not.

incorrect.explanation: switchport trunk native vlan 10 sets the untagged VLAN — not the allowed list.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: native vlan limits allowed VLANs
incorrect.whatItDoes: switchport trunk native vlan 10 expects VLAN tags on a link that should behave as access-only in this stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Trunk vs access (allowed vlans): switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 carries VLAN tags on inter-switch links — switchport trunk native vlan 10 describes access-port behavior.

answerReview.examTip: Trunk pruning: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30 — verify with show interfaces trunk.
